benchmark_note: Published payroll expectations are not unique. The current Trading Economics calendar snapshot shows 45K, while Wolfe Research published 65K on Aug. 25 and AP reporting on Sep. 1 also cited forecasts around 65K. These differences are preserved rather than selecting a favorable benchmark after resolution.
resolution_rule: Use the first U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation release for August 2026 scheduled for 2026-09-04 at 08:30 ET. Resolve TRUE only if first-release total nonfarm payroll employment changes by 25000 jobs or less AND the first-release unemployment rate is 4.2% or higher at BLS published precision; otherwise FALSE. Score the 0.32 joint-event probability with Brier and log loss. Score the 38000 payroll point and 4.2% unemployment point separately by absolute error against the same first-release values and against each frozen point benchmark. Record separate 80% interval coverage for payrolls and unemployment. Do not substitute later payroll revisions, benchmark revisions, or a consensus captured after the evidence cutoff.
rationale: July JOLTS provides direct low-hire/low-fire evidence: hires fell to 5.054 million and quits fell while layoffs/discharges also declined to 1.666 million. This raises the chance of weak payroll creation without yet implying a layoff-driven collapse.

August ISM manufacturing employment remained expansionary at 51.2 and total manufacturing output remained solid, while initial claims have stayed low. These observations keep the joint broad-deterioration event below even odds rather than making it the base case.

Housing/construction remain weak and JOLTS June openings were revised materially lower, so the model's payroll point is set below the stronger 65K external forecast and modestly below the current 45K calendar consensus.

The joint event is intentionally more discriminating than payrolls alone: weak payroll creation with unemployment at or above 4.2% would strengthen H002 more than a low payroll number accompanied by stable unemployment and low layoffs.
surprising_if: First-release payrolls are >=125000 while unemployment is <=4.1%, indicating substantially stronger labor demand than the low-hire/low-fire state expects.
First-release payrolls are <=-50000 while unemployment is >=4.3%, indicating synchronized deterioration much stronger than the current H002 weight allows.
